comment: Seccomp profile for dai/superset:v2.1 (base: python:3.10-slim-trixie, multi-stage rebase from apache/superset:latest). Covers superset-init / superset (gunicorn) containers. Allows all Docker-default syscalls and additionally blocks a general-purpose hardening baseline (mount, kernel module loading, kexec, cross-process memory introspection, BPF/perf, swap/hostname, obsolete syscalls). NOTE: the 6 OS-layer HIGH CVEs covered by sast/report/superset_v2_vulner_report.md (libncursesw6/libtinfo6/ncurses-base/ncurses-bin CVE-2025-69720 terminal-handling buffer overflow; libsqlite3-0 CVE-2026-11822/CVE-2026-11824 memory corruption) are application/library-internal logic bugs triggered through normal C function calls (terminfo parsing, SQL parsing), not through a distinguishable raw syscall -- seccomp cannot filter at that granularity. The CVE-specific containment for these 6 findings is implemented via docker-compose_vm5_secure.yml (read_only root filesystem makes the terminfo/sqlite write-paths structurally unreachable regardless of LSM, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges) and via Superset's own PREVENT_UNSAFE_DB_CONNECTIONS=True default (see secure_report/superset_secure_report.md). No AppArmor/SELinux custom policy is used (RHEL 9 production runs under Docker's default SELinux container_t confinement with no custom type authored). This seccomp profile is therefore general defense-in-depth, not a CVE-2025-69720/CVE-2026-11822/CVE-2026-11824-specific control.

syscalls.comment: Block mount-related syscalls. Superset (gunicorn/Flask) never mounts filesystems at runtime.
Block kernel module loading (container should never load kernel modules)
Block cross-process memory access / ptrace (no debugger or process introspection needed at runtime; also closes off a common post-exploitation primitive)
Block BPF and perf events (privilege escalation / info leakage primitives, not used by gunicorn/Flask)
Block swap and hostname changes (not needed by Superset)
Block obsolete/legacy syscalls not needed by Superset (oprofile dcookie lookup, legacy NFS server control, x86 vm86 mode). General attack-surface reduction.
